players.product: AI data-center campus leases on converted Bitcoin-mining power sites (Sandersville GA 175 MW critical IT on a 20-year triple net lease, tenant undisclosed; Sealy and Brazoria TX under exclusivity)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matt Schultz: CleanSpark has amassed a portfolio of 35 different sites around the country. At Sandersville, Georgia, where it has operated for almost four years with 11 exahash of Bitcoin mining, it built a fully energized substation with 250 megawatts of power. The tenant requested a specific EPCM that has built for it before and manufactures much of the mechanical, electrical and plumbing components internally; CleanSpark entered into a lump sum turnkey contract that contemplates the first data hall will be delivered in December of 2027, pushing some of the potential risks and liquidated damages to the construction side. Because the EPCM builds the vast majority of the data center in a factory (an assembly-line process) under a fixed price lump sum contract, Schultz's expectation is 10, 11 million a megawatt complete RFS on the data center.
quarterly_data.figure: 35 sites; 250 megawatts energized substation at Sandersville; first data hall delivery December 2027 under a lump sum turnkey contract; 10, 11 million a megawatt complete RFS

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matt Schultz: impressed by the community's flexibility at Sandersville, the same tenant asked for exclusivity on other parts of CleanSpark's portfolio and entered a short duration exclusivity on up to 885 additional megawatts in Texas, of which 585 megawatts was recently announced to be Batch Zero base load, so the energization timelines meet the tenant's expectations. 'We feel very confident that the exclusivity period and the option for that will ultimately be executed, and we're seeing price go up in parallel with demand.' He added that rates for long-term leases are increasing and appreciating rapidly.
quarterly_data.figure: up to 885 MW in Texas under exclusivity (585 MW Batch Zero base load)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matt Schultz: in Cheyenne, Wyoming, CleanSpark won 110 megawatts from Black Hills Energy in an RFP where the other bidder was a trillion-dollar hyperscaler, because it could deploy immersion-cooled Bitcoin mining infrastructure on a modular basis and start paying a power bill in 90 days; it has bought enough land to build a proper data center to monetize those megawatts when it has the right client, built to that client's reference architecture and basis of design.

CEO Matt Schultz does not see an AI infrastructure bubble ('hard no, from my perspective'). He sees three constraints: capital (money flows where there is the least risk and the highest credit certainty), energy availability (energized megawatts; hyperscalers are contemplating behind-the-meter investments in building their own power plants) and delivery certainty, which the high yield market now treats as the predominant factor in its willingness to provide credit and in the rates. He called data-center siting a political issue after the Texas governor's action and said CleanSpark and its EPCM provider ran an educational roadshow in Texas on dark sky issues, water usage, ambient noise and utility-rate impacts.
